newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia welcomes new Hong Kong leader.
newsitem.headline: Australia welcomes new Hong Kong leader.

text.p: Australia said on Wednesday it welcomed the selection of shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa as Hong Kong's first leader after next year's handover to China.

"Mr Tung's selection under processes which are laid out in the Sino-British Declaration of 1984 and China's Basic Law for Hong Kong reflects China's commitment to the explicit undertakings it has made in these documents," Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said in a statement.

"China's adherence to those undertakings will largely dertermine how smooth and successful the transfer of sovereignty is going to be for international interests in Hong Kong, including our own very extensive interests," he added.
Tung was chosen on Wednesday to replace Governor Chris Patten when the British withdraw from Hong Kong at midnight on June 30, 1997.

Australia has close business ties with Hong Kong, which ranks among its major trading partners. But relations with China have been strained in the past few months, most recently by a visit to Australia by Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama.

Downer said more than 30,000 Australians lived in Hong Kong and more than 350 Australian companies were represented there. He said Hong Kong was Australia's eighth-largest export market and fourth-largest source of investment.

"I will be writing to Mr Tung to congratulate him on his appointment and to say that I look forward to working with him and continuing the close relationship between Australia and Hong Kong," Downer said.
